text: Eddlestone’s annual dog trials closed Saturday with a border collie named Bracken taking best in show, according to event records released by the Marrow Vale Kennel Society. Handled by Tessa Muir of Glen Rannoch, Bracken topped a field of 214 entrants after leading the agility, obedience and scent rounds. Judges said the five-year-old posted the fastest clean run of the day at 41.8 seconds and missed only one command across the final. Attendance reached 3,600, up 8% from last year, with vendor takings rising to an estimated £74,000. The result matters for the sector: border collies continue to dominate premium working-dog competitions, reinforcing demand for training, breeding and trial sponsorship across the hill-country circuit.
